cells.tense: You are feeling your way into what's next, and the ground under you is bearing it well.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Pick some small care you want to keep alive and give it fifteen unhurried minutes today, then the same again tomorrow — nothing bigger, nothing that has to prove itself.
cells.core:
What you sense coming is met with a beginner's openness, and the ground under it holds. That pairing is rarer than it sounds. You can feel toward something that hasn't happened yet without going brittle or stiff, and here the sensing and the bearing work as one, with no strain showing.

Let the care build slowly. A little today, a little more tomorrow, no bonfire. Direction comes from what you genuinely feel, and what you feel has somewhere solid to land. Nothing has to burn down to prove it's real. Feed it once, then trust what's under you to carry the rest.

Small and steady beats bright and brief.
cells.sheetLine: Steady beats bright. Keep it small and alive.
cells.verb: Open to what is coming before you know what it is
cells.place: Where you hold the weight of what must be borne

cells.tense: You will have braced for a feeling that hasn't arrived, and your body is already carrying it.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Choose something you're shouldering and give it five unhurried minutes of finding out what it needs, before you plan what happens next with it.
cells.core:
The feeling ahead is being carried before it lands. You see a hundred ways it could go and your body bears every one at once — heavier than any single outcome would be. Strength that serves you is turning into a way of bracing, and the bracing tires out what could simply wait. What looks like staying ready is really staying clenched.

Let one growing thing teach you what it needs. Not the whole future — just the next bit, tended once, without forcing it to bloom. When you start watching instead of appeasing, the weight changes. That watching is what you're good at. It was the part that held, before it started holding everything.

Something small, tended, tells you more than a forecast can.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that had already closed, and your hands were still holding its frame.
cells.act: follow a raw curiosity with no use for it
cells.ask: Follow one curiosity that has no purpose yet — something you want to know for no reason — for twenty minutes, and stop wherever that carries you.
cells.core:
Something that needed feeling was held instead, and then the bearing became the whole job. The wonder that used to move you spent itself on what already happened, and the present has been kept at arm's length because your arms were full. You still have the strength to bear what's here — it hasn't gone anywhere — but it's been holding what's finished.

Curiosity will do what effort can't. Follow a small wanting-to-know with nothing attached and see where it carries you. The dull place doesn't need you to push feeling into it; it gets its current back from what you actually want to know. Start anywhere your attention actually leans and see what shows up.

cells.tense: You have been bearing things for people without noticing it's your strength doing the work.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Take what you've been bearing quietly and put it on paper, then follow the line of it — what happened, what happened after — before you decide what any of it meant.
cells.core:
The endurance under other people is yours, and your version has it as ordinary background. You talk about it like the furniture. The strength that doesn't break or go stiff has been holding more than anyone sees, and the freshness you bring to each new feeling is still there underneath the habit. Nothing about that strength is small.

Give it a record. Set what you've been quietly shouldering onto paper, plain, without the feeling words, and follow where the method leads you. The discipline isn't cold — it's the earlier form of the same tenderness, and it serves you rather than emptying you. You were holding before you knew you were.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person opens to feeling with fresh, wide-eyed trust — a stance the record cannot verify in their life. A reader could reasonably say that what looks like fresh wonder is actually a practiced endurance, and that they have been holding things far longer than they let on. The ask survives being wrong: tending a small thing once teaches them whether the balance was real or performed, either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the one about wonder — it flatters the card rather than seating it in Fortitude.
